title: Find, Replace and Go To Special
summary: Wildcards, and selecting blanks, constants or formulas in one go.
objectives: Find and replace text across a sheet, safely.
Use Match entire cell contents and wildcards.
Select every blank (or every formula) with Go To Special, and fill blanks at once.

p: **Ctrl+F** finds. **Ctrl+H** finds and replaces every match in one go.
Excel tells you how many replacements it made.
Before Replace All, think: what else might match?
In real life: Renamed “Bombay” to “Mumbai” across 3,000 delivery rows with one Replace All.

p: **Ctrl+Enter** puts one entry into every selected cell at once.
Works with 0, a word, or a formula like =B2 that copies the value above.
In real life: Marked 300 skipped answers as “No response” in seconds.

why.0: Enter fills only the active cell.

demo.intro: Replace old city names across the list, carefully.

steps.say: Old names, “Bombay” and “Calcutta”, are scattered down column C. Press Ctrl+H to open Find and Replace.
Find *Bombay*, replace with *Mumbai*, Replace All: three cells change.
For Bangalore, tick **Match entire cell contents**, so “12 Bangalore Road” stays as it is.

demo.outro: Replace All is powerful. Entire-cell matching keeps it safe.

lab.intro: Update the city names with Find and Replace (Ctrl+H, or the 🔍 button). Tick Match entire cell contents where it matters.

tasks.prompt: Replace every **Bombay** in the City column with **Mumbai**.
Change the city **Bangalore** to **Bengaluru**, but leave the address “12 Bangalore Road” in D5 as it is.
hints: A plain replace would change the address too.

tasks.prompt: Which search finds both **Shah** and **Shaikh** in the Customer column?
hints: Think about the wildcard for “any characters”.
tasks.explain: `*` stands for any number of characters, so `Sh*` matches names starting with Sh.

tasks.prompt: Three customers have no phone number. Fastest way to put “Not given” in all the blanks at once?
hints: Think about selecting only the empty cells.
Go To Special can do that.
Then type once and use Ctrl+Enter.
options: Select B2:B8, Go To Special › Blanks, type Not given, Ctrl+Enter
Replace All with an empty Find

real.title: Fill blanks with Go To Special
steps: Press **F5 › Special › Blanks › OK**. Only the empty cells stay selected.

quiz.q: Which shortcut opens Find and Replace with the Replace tab ready?
What does `?` match in a Find?
quiz.explain: `?` is one character; `*` is any number.

quiz.q: What does Go To Special › Formulas select?
quiz.explain: Handy for checking which cells are calculated and which are typed.

quiz.q: Which key enters the same value into every selected cell?
Replace All changed “Pune” inside “Punekar Traders” too. What option would have prevented it?

points: **Ctrl+H**: find and replace across the sheet; check what else might match.
**Match entire cell contents** avoids partial matches; `*` and `?` are wildcards.
**F5 › Special › Blanks**, type, **Ctrl+Enter** fills every gap at once.
recap.cheat: Ctrl+H to replace, entire-cell matching to stay safe, Ctrl+Enter to fill a selection.
